content: Both parents are my own designs; ligand 1 is the best-jnk3 molecule at 0.43 and I know its atom table, so atom 19 is the cap cyclopropane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 1 over a non-ring bond - the anchor that lets me rebuild the whole molecule in one modification. The lever I have not touched at all is the central benzene. The only substituent I ever put there was a fluorine, which cost 0.01-0.05, and I generalised from that to avoid decorating it - but a fluorine is small, strongly electron-withdrawing and a poor proxy for substitution in general. A methyl is the opposite on every count except size, so it is the right second data point: if it also costs activity, the central ring genuinely wants to be bare and I can stop; if it gains, there is a pocket there worth exploring. I am putting it ortho to the anilide nitrogen and meta to the arylamine, which keeps it away from both donors. Expected product: the 4-methylpyridine cyclopropanecarboxamide with an extra ring methyl, about 267 Da.
